title: 12 Reasons Your Wife Needs Her Mother More Than You Need That Promotion
author: Anthony B. Bradley
summary: Synthesizing more than a dozen peer-reviewed studies from evolutionary biology, sociology, and developmental psychology, Anthony Bradley makes the case that proximity to the maternal grandmother is one of the most empirically powerful family welfare interventions available to a husband. When a maternal grandmother dies or moves away, maternal employment drops by 27 percent; her presence buffers children against adverse childhood events; she frees mothers for direct childcare by absorbing heavy domestic tasks; and she is the one relative whose positive effect on child survival appears across 69% of the studies that examined her—no other kin category comes close. The grandmother effect is not a relic of pre-industrial life—it adapts across modern and traditional societies. The mother-daughter bond is not incidental to caregiving; it is the infrastructure on which caregiving is built. The practical implication: a husband who moves his family away from his wife's mother for a promotion may be sacrificing $75,000 to $120,000 in childcare savings in the first five years alone, plus the incalculable support benefits no daycare can replicate.
points: When a maternal grandmother dies, maternal employment falls by 12 percentage points—a 27% decline—while fathers' employment is unaffected, confirming that grandmothers provide irreplaceable childcare infrastructure.
Proximity to a maternal grandmother saves families $75,000–$120,000 in childcare costs in the first five years alone, not counting emotional, health, and workforce participation benefits.

Maternal grandmother involvement significantly reduces emotional and behavioral problems in grandchildren who have experienced multiple adverse childhood events—her presence can shift high-adversity children to look like low-adversity children on key measures.
In Sear and Mace's cross-cultural review of 45 studies spanning every inhabited continent, the maternal grandmother improved child survival in 69% of studies—no other relative came close.
The maternal grandmother's caregiving advantage over paternal grandparents maps onto genetic certainty: she is the one grandparent with zero uncertain links to the grandchild.
quotes: One of the best ways a man can provide for his family is to do whatever is necessary to make sure his wife lives in the same city as her mother, assuming they have a good relationship.
Civilization would not exist without them, and the social science shows us exactly why families thrive when mothers live in close proximity to maternal grandmothers.

There is no financial advisor in America who would tell a young family to ignore a $75,000 to $120,000 savings opportunity. But that is exactly what happens when a husband moves his wife across the country for a promotion without weighing what proximity to her mother is worth.
Among children with high adversity exposure, those with an involved maternal grandmother looked more like children with low adversity exposure on key behavioral measures.

The maternal grandmother improved child survival in 69% of the studies that examined her role, nine out of thirteen. No other kin category came close. Maternal grandmothers are not helpful because of any one cultural norm. Something deeper is at work.
The mother-daughter bond is not incidental to caregiving. It is the infrastructure on which caregiving is built.
